subject: Request: adjust service-commitment floor & monthly remedy schedule for batched endpoints
messages:
From: Simon Walters <simon.walters@finedge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Li <maya.li@finedge.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Service commitments for batched endpoints — ask

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput gains look promising. Before we finalize the PO we need to align on two items in the template SLA that are blocking procurement: the uptime floor and the monthly service credit cap when we run large scheduled batches.

Our concerns in short:
- We accept the 99.95% baseline for interactive endpoints, but our backfill/batched workloads (daily windows where we push heavy inference throughput) introduce predictable p95 latency spikes and short saturation events. Those windows are tolerated operationally, but the current SLA treats any monthly deviation the same way and it could trigger outsized credits we can’t account for in forecasting.
- We’d like an explicit latency floor for batched endpoints (e.g., carveout that allows p95 to exceed interactive thresholds during scheduled batch windows) and an amendment to the monthly credit schedule that limits credits tied to batched workload degradation to a defined cap (we suggested 8% of the monthly invoice).

Two asks: can Redwood provide a redline to the standard template that: 1) adds a scheduled-batch latency carveout with definition of “scheduled window”, and 2) adds a differentiated credit bucket (separate from interactive endpoints) with a capped monthly remedy?

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through expected traffic patterns and examples.

Best,
Simon
Simon Walters
Head of Platform Operations — FinEdge
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Simon Walters <simon.walters@finedge.com>
Cc: Maya Li <maya.li@finedge.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Service commitments for batched endpoints — ask

Simon — thanks for the clear summary and for flagging the predictable nature of your batched jobs. We can definitely propose a tailored amendment. High-level options we typically offer:

1) Scheduled-batch carveout: define scheduled windows (recurring times or calendar-driven), exempt those windows from the interactive p95 latency SLO, and instead measure against a batch-specific SLO.

2) Differentiated remedy pool: split monthly remedy into two buckets (interactive + batch). For batched pool we can set a lower percentage cap (we've done 5–10% in past pilots) and add an operational cap so credits cannot exceed X% of the batch invoice line item.

3) Maintenance/failover carveouts and throttling tolerance: formalize thresholds for autoscale/queueing backpressure and acceptable transient saturation periods.

I’ll draft a proposed redline and include a short runbook language for what counts as a scheduled window (cron, calendar invite, or explicit API call to mark start/end). PrIyom / Marissa — looping you both for legal and CS input on the credit language and runbook wording.

Simon — can you share an example week (CSV of hourly qps + p95) and preferred scheduled window definitions? That will help us craft realistic caps. I’ve attached a first-pass skeleton (redwood_sla_amendment_v1.docx) and a sample runbook excerpt (batched-latency-runbook.pdf).

Two next steps: 1) you send the traffic snippet, 2) we iterate the redline and aim to have a countersigned amendment for the PO. If helpful, 30-min call on Monday morning to finalize.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Feb 2025 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: draft language thoughts (internal)

Kimberly — quick notes on the attachment and proposed approach from legal/CS perspective:

- Acceptable: carveout that is explicitly scheduled and customer‑initiated (we need an API flag or calendar IDs so we can validate).
- Remedy cap: OK to offer a separate batch bucket capped at 10% of the monthly invoice for those endpoints, provided we limit the scope to named endpoints and add an aggregate cap (so combined interactive + batch credits don’t exceed 15% of invoice).
- Measurement: require both parties to agree on the telemetry sources. We should call out preferred metrics (Redwood request logs + customer-supplied telemetry) and an arbitration clause for disputes.
- Maintenance carveouts: keep the standard maintenance carveouts but allow an additional scheduled maintenance window for batch jobs if the customer notifies 48 hours prior.

I drafted inline language in redwood_sla_amendment_v1.docx (see section 3.2–3.5). Marissa, can you add a short operational note about how CS will support marking windows and any runbook expectations?

— PrIyom
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Simon Walters <simon.walters@finedge.com>
Cc: Maya Li <maya.li@finedge.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Feb 2025 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed amendment + next steps (attached)

Simon — thanks for the traffic sample you sent this morning; that made drafting straightforward. Attached is the proposed amendment (redwood_sla_amendment_v1.docx) and the short runbook excerpt we discussed (batched-latency-runbook.pdf). Summary of the key points in plain language:

- Interactive endpoints remain on 99.95% monthly uptime, measured per standard template.
- Batched endpoints (explicitly named in Schedule A) will be placed into a separate performance bucket. During customer-declared scheduled windows (calendar invite, cron rule, or the new /v1/batches/start API flag) the interactive latency SLO is suspended and replaced by a batch SLO: p95 latency <= 2x interactive p95 (or an absolute threshold of 1s for heavy models), whichever is lower.
- Remedy structure: batch performance shortfalls are remediated from a separate bucket capped at 10% of the monthly invoice for the named batch endpoints. Combined remedy cap across interactive + batch will not exceed 15% of invoice.
- Measurement & dispute resolution: Redwood’s telemetry will be primary for calculations; customer telemetry may be submitted within 10 business days and we’ll use a jointly‑appointed SME to reconcile discrepancies.
- Operational commitments: customers must notify Redwood 48 hours before planned heavy batch windows or mark the window with the API; failure to mark will default to interactive SLOs for the period.

If this aligns with FinEdge’s needs we can: 1) incorporate any small edits you want, 2) run the DocuSign flow (link included), and 3) provision the API flagging in staging for you to exercise prior to go-live.

If you want a short call to walk the amendment, happy to schedule — Monday/Tuesday next week looks open on my calendar.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this.

Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198
